Overall, Duolingo is a fun learning app with features that keep me motivated in learning a new language. I love the variety of courses available: many different languages, chess, math, and music.

However, I am not a fan of the energy system. It doesn’t provide enough for the user in certain situations.

For example, I wanted to try Legendary mode on a course that I was confident in. The first time, I missed one question…then ended up running out of energy when I had only one or two more questions for me to clear it. I had to stop the challenge because of this.

I did this same challenge a few days later. This time, I did not miss any questions; however, I still would’ve run out of energy if I hadn’t been lucky enough for Duo to replenish just enough before the question prior to the last. For both of these tries, I started with full energy.

With the old hearts system, this would not have been a problem. Also, the hearts system encouraged me to learn at my own pace. With the energy system, it’s more difficult to move on ahead when I’m ready. Sure, I could try skipping forward to the next unit, but I would rather be able to complete the challenges in the unit I’m currently on before that.

One more problem that the energy system amplifies is the rewards for completing daily quests. It seems that, more often than not, the treasure chest holds an EXP boost for ~15 minutes or so. If you don’t have enough energy to complete a lesson, the point feels moot.

This next part concerns the Japanese language course, but it may apply to other courses as well. With the most recent update, I feel like too many of the exercises rely on the user speaking, rather than typing or matching. It feels like nearly half of the exercises are speaking ones! Speaking exercises can also be frustrating because there are some words that it frequently does not register as me speaking correctly, when I am saying that word exactly as it is pronounced.

Additionally, I feel several of the non-speaking exercises have been watered down in difficulty. The question may give me a scenario and ask me to fill in a word or phrase in a multiple choice style question. This isn’t necessarily bad, especially for exercises earlier on in a unit, but I feel like there’s too many types of this exercise for later in a unit.

I’d still recommend Duolingo for those wanting to learn a language, chess, etc. It definitely keeps learning fun and motivating. Still, I prefer some aspects that have since been removed.

I also have to agree with some complaints given in other comments. It’s annoying how some ads are difficult to close because the X button in the corner is so tiny. Finally, some aspects of this app are not entirely kid-friendly, despite the app marketing itself as such.

review_title: 2000+ Day Streak. Can’t Speak a Lick of Spanish
review_text: Been using Duolingo 5+ years straight, every day, and I can’t speak a lick of Spanish. At this point I stick with it out of habit.  I’m using other apps and videos to help with speaking. I’m not paying extra for the AI upgrade, given the poor results I’ve had with the normal product.
Energy system sucks, can only do 2 lessons a day because of it. uninstalled
The one word English translations are sometimes bad because that one word can have several meanings. Without context you can’t tell what word is intended. The app also often crashes after long use.

The story lessons drive me insane. I wish it were possible to speed them up, maybe even listen to them at a native speed as an option, especially at the more advanced levels. The fact that my story at level 115 French unfolds at the same speed as my level 12 Italian and Catalan and level 10 Hawaiian is absurd.

A great learning language app if you are constantly always learning. For example, if you don’t go on for maybe three days and you don’t do you’re course, they decided to give you a course refresher or something like that. It’s fine and all but they gave me words that I have no idea how to spell, say, or I just don’t know in general. It’s frustrating and annoying because I don’t know the words yet they still give it do me. So yeah, it’s a great learning app with many languages and tools to help you learn but sometimes it really doesn’t help. I’ve wanted to delete the app many times out of frustration. It’s not the best but not the worst either so I’d give it three stars.

I did those extra topic lessons hoping they will catch me up, but no, some words were introduced, but very sporadically, no way to retain and solidify the knowledge similar to the words from before this awful update. Also, those extra lessons were only for about 10% of all the new material that was dumped.

review_title: The very BEST for ALL  BEGINNERS.
review_text:
Hola, yo soy Natalie. 
I just recently started learning Spanish and I’m loving this app. It’s easy and teaches you to read, write, and speak the language with ease. I love it so much that my bath water is freezing before I’m ready to put DUOLINGO away. And I yell at the kids for hogging the bathroom. Thankfully they are all asleep.  Momma’s gonna get her “Duolingo” on. 
I just wanted to say that the creators have done an amazing job with this app. Gracias.

Overall, Duolingo is a great app, fun, interesting, informative, and really can help you learn languages and more. 

My one critique would be the lack of organization. I am on the chess track and it would be nice if the lessons were more focused on specific things like openings and other concepts. It seems to bounce around a lot and doesn’t really go into openings at all. That said, I have improved significantly as a chess player on Duolingo.
